captions.text: Ever wonder why your coding agent did what it did?
The model sees far more than you typed:
a system prompt, tool definitions, reminders slipped between your turns.
You never see it, and almost none of it is documented.
It's written by the harness: the program around the model, like Claude Code or Codex/ChatGPT.
Harness Source Map reads all of it out of the shipped apps.
How does plan mode stop Claude Code from editing?
Here's the exact reminder it inserts, and where it ships.
The same for Codex/ChatGPT,
including GPT-6's persistent-mode instructions.
What wins shows which setting Claude Code obeys.
Anthropic can flip this flag without a release;
your environment variable still wins.
That's what the harness can send.
Trace shows what it actually sent, in your own session:
1 day 4 hours, 90 subagents.
Time runs left to right.
Height is how much text the model had in front of it.
Gray is the harness, pink is what it injected, green is you.
Zoom in: each request is a stack of these layers.
Open the pink one: instructions from your MCP servers, never shown in your chat.
Here, under a tenth came from you.
Almost half came from the harness.
Search the session: your CLAUDE.md went out 94 times,
to 91 agents, the main thread and every subagent.
Press 2 for everything that left your machine.
Open a deploy to see why it ran:
you asked for it mid-turn, and bypassPermissions let it through.
The log still leaves things out.
Record a short session's network traffic, attach the capture, and Trace lines it up with the log.
Now see what the model was really sent:
a billing header in the system prompt,
all 18 tools,
and a 45,000-character system message.
None of it is in your log.
And where your data went:
your login token to 2 Anthropic hosts,
your device details to Datadog.
Every flag your account was served: 728.
Click one to see what it turns on:
“When you have enough information to act, act.”
Harness Source Map.
It runs in your browser.
See what your agent was really told.
